about.title: Temple City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Temple City households buy and use ordinary products every day — kitchen appliances, tools, car parts, furniture, children's items — and most work exactly as expected. When one doesn't, the injuries can range from minor burns to serious, life-altering harm. California generally treats these claims under strict liability, meaning an injured person typically doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was defective and that the defect caused the harm. That single distinction can matter a great deal in how a claim is built and who can be named as a defendant, since manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share responsibility. Our team reviews product liability claims involving defects and can explain the strict liability framework as it applies to your specific product, and advise on preserving the item itself as evidence while next steps are sorted out.

whyChoose.title: Why Temple City Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Fight
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an injured person generally focuses on the product's condition rather than trying to prove a manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer that sold the item can potentially be held liable, giving us more than one avenue to pursue on a claim.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Guidance Matters Early
items.desc: Since the product itself is often central evidence, reaching out quickly can help make sure it's kept intact and not repaired, discarded, or altered before it's examined.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California often applies strict liability to defective product claims, which generally means you need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless. We can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought near Las Tunas Drive or Rosemead Boulevard in Temple City — does the location matter?
items.answer: The location of the purchase itself isn't usually the deciding factor in a product defect claim, but details like where and when you bought the item, and any receipts or packaging, can help support the case. What matters most is preserving the product and documenting the injury. Our team can walk through exactly what records would help.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if possible — don't repair, clean, or throw it away. The product is often key evidence in a strict liability claim. Contact us and we can advise on how to preserve it properly.
